subject: general
question:
Which of the given values can x NOT take without changing the mode in the following data set?

{1, 2, 3, 3, 7, 8, 9, 3, 11, x, 17, 11, 13}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mode = most frequent value → currently 3 appears 3 times

Check closest competitor: 11 appears 2 times

If x = 11 → frequency of 11 becomes 3 → tie with 3

This changes uniqueness of mode

**∴ Answer = 11**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

{1, 2, 3, 3, 7, 8, 9, 3, 11, x, 17, 11, 13}

**Formula used:**

Mode = value with highest frequency

**Calculation:**

⇒ Frequency of 3 = 3

⇒ Frequency of 11 = 2

⇒ All others appear once

⇒ If x = 3 → frequency becomes 4 → mode remains 3

⇒ If x = 11 → frequency becomes 3 → two modes (3 and 11)

⇒ Mode changes (no longer unique)

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mode Concept

Mode is the value that appears most frequently in a dataset.

Unique vs Multiple Mode

If two values share highest frequency → bimodal set.

Effect of Adding One Value

Adding a number can increase its frequency and may change the mode.

Frequency Check Trick

Always compare highest and second-highest frequencies to predict changes.
